question: Compare the agriculture/fishing and manufacturing panels in Figure 5.11 between 2010 and 2020. Which sector loses workers and which gains, and what skill color dominates agriculture?
answer:
In Figure 5.11, comparing the agriculture and fishing and manufacturing panels between 2010 and 2020, agriculture and fishing loses workers (decreasing from nearly 25 million to roughly 17.5 million), while manufacturing gains workers (increasing from around 7 million to roughly 11.5 million). [p161-figure-5.11]

In agriculture and fishing, the dominant skill colors are yellow (unskilled manual) and grey (skilled manual), with yellow/unskilled manual being the largest segment in 2010 and yellow and grey dominating the panel overall. [p161-figure-5.11]

events.answer:
In Figure 5.11, between 2010 and 2020, agriculture and fishing loses workers (total number of workers decreases from nearly 25 million to around 17.5 million), while manufacturing gains workers (total number of workers increases from around 7 million to over 11 million). [p161-figure-5.11]

The skill color that dominates agriculture in Figure 5.11 is yellow (representing unskilled manual) and grey (representing skilled manual). Specifically, unskilled manual (yellow) and skilled manual (grey) dominate, but looking closely at the total bars, yellow (unskilled manual) is the largest component in 2010 and both grey and yellow dominate the stack across years. [p161-figure-5.11]

model_claims.text: In Figure 5.11, between 2010 and 2020, agriculture and fishing loses workers (total number of workers decreases from nearly 25 million to around 17.5 million), while manufacturing gains workers (total number of workers increases from around 7 million to over 11 million).

Specifically, unskilled manual (yellow) and skilled manual (grey) dominate, but looking closely at the total bars, yellow (unskilled manual) is the largest component in 2010 and both grey and yellow dominate the stack across years.
